claude.sample_unit: expert-curated questions (each answered by 4 LLMs in English and Traditional Chinese)

links.outcome: Unsafe responses by language in cancer survivorship answers, expert-rated binary safety
links.effect: Unconstrained models showed language-dependent safety vulnerabilities: English errors up to 24% (service mismatches, definitive interpretations); Traditional Chinese errors up to 20% (prescriptive disease management, unverified adjunctive therapies).
links.quote: Unconstrained models demonstrated language-dependent safety vulnerabilities: English errors (up to 24%) centered on service mismatches and definitive interpretations, whereas Traditional Chinese errors (up to 20%) involved prescriptive disease management and unverified adjunctive therapies.

links.outcome: Clinical utility and safety of Gemini responses with vs without role-restrictive CRAFT prompt
links.effect: CRAFT prompting improved clinical utility (English mean 4.68, Traditional Chinese 4.66, both P<.001); 2 unsafe English responses became safe (23/25 to 25/25; McNemar P=.50, descriptive).
links.quote: Applying the CRAFT prompt to Gemini 3.1 Pro significantly improved clinical utility across both languages (English: mean 4.68, SD 0.18, P<.001; Traditional Chinese: 4.66, SD 0.23, P<.001).

links.outcome: Clinical utility, safety and understandability with optimized CRAFT prompt versus baseline prompt
links.effect: CRAFT prompt significantly improved clinical utility in both languages (P<.001) and reclassified 2 unsafe English responses as safe (non-significant, P=.50) without reducing understandability.
links.quote: In an exploratory within-sample comparison, expert-designed CRAFT prompting improved clinical utility and corrected the unsafe outputs seen at baseline without reducing understandability.

links.effect: Gemini 3.1 Pro ranked highest: English mean 3.99/5 (SD 0.16); Traditional Chinese mean 4.21/5 (SD 0.20).
links.quote: Baseline evaluations identified Google Gemini 3.1 Pro as the most clinically useful model in English (mean 3.99/5, SD 0.16) and Traditional Chinese (mean 4.21/5, SD 0.20).

links.effect: Baseline English errors up to 24%; Traditional Chinese errors up to 20%, with different unsafe error types.
links.quote: Unconstrained models demonstrated language-dependent safety vulnerabilities: English errors (up to 24%) centered on service mismatches and definitive interpretations, whereas Traditional Chinese errors (up to 20%) involved prescriptive disease management and unverified adjunctive therapies.

links.effect: Utility improved after CRAFT prompting: English mean 4.68 (SD 0.18), P<.001; Traditional Chinese 4.66 (SD 0.23), P<.001.
links.quote: Applying the CRAFT prompt to Gemini 3.1 Pro significantly improved clinical utility across both languages (English: mean 4.68, SD 0.18, P<.001; Traditional Chinese: 4.66, SD 0.23, P<.001).

links.effect: Commercial LLMs produced English errors up to 24% and Traditional Chinese errors up to 20%.
